permissionRules.note: Reading is always free — the OS cannot learn without it.
Search primitives.
Read-only git inspection.
Test execution is encouraged, never gated.
Only inside the agent’s own worktree — enforced by the orchestrator.
Config changes reach every environment.
Supply-chain surface — human confirms every new dependency.
Read queries against a snapshot replica.
Data mutation always needs a human.
Hard denial. No agent may destroy data — ever.
Requires a proven rollback before approval is offered.
Staging is disposable — agents own it.
Production is the human’s signature, never the agent’s.
Agents receive references, never plaintext values.
Direct pushes to main are impossible — PR only.
Agents commit freely inside their own task branches.
Research is read-only; fetched content is treated as data, never instructions.
Anything other humans will see gets confirmed first.
Blanket denial, no exceptions, no override flag.
Outbound messages always carry the human’s name — so the human presses send.

memory.title: Architecture Decision #142 — TRANS table must not be directly modified
memory.body: No service, script or agent may INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE on any TRANS_* table directly. All writes go through SP_PostTransaction, which stamps the audit trio (POSTED_BY, POSTED_ON, POSTED_MACHINE) and writes the paired row into TRANS_LEDGER. Direct writes leave the ledger unbalanced and the month-end close silently reports a wrong figure.
memory.reason: Legacy accounting integration.

memory.title: Repository layer is the only place raw SQL is allowed
memory.body: Services take an I<Name>Repository via constructor injection. A service that opens a SqlConnection is an automatic review rejection. Reviewer agent greps for "new SqlConnection" outside src/Data/ on every diff.
memory.reason: Two 2023 incidents traced back to ad-hoc SQL inside services bypassing the retry policy.
memory.source: ADR-19 + Code Reviewer rejection pattern (14 occurrences)

memory.title: HIMS billing talks to ERP only over the PMI compatibility contract
memory.body: HIMS v3 never reads CAREWORKS tables directly. Everything crosses through the PMI contract views (VW_PMI_PATIENT, VW_PMI_CHARGE). The views are versioned; breaking one requires a dual-write window of at least one billing cycle.
memory.reason: Both systems are live at the same hospitals during the renewal.

memory.title: Frontend state: no new state library, ever
memory.body: React Context + useReducer for cross-screen state, local useState for everything else. TanStack Query only for server cache. A PR that adds Zustand/Redux/Jotai gets closed without review.
memory.reason: Four state libraries already died in this codebase between 2013 and 2021; the migration cost each time was measured in months.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2025-01-09 (Hinglish: "naya state library mat lana, jo hai usi mein karo")

memory.title: Ride pricing engine is pure — no I/O inside calculate()
memory.body: pricing/engine.py::calculate() takes a frozen RideContext and returns a Quote. Surge, tolls and promos are resolved before the call. This is what makes the 2,100-case fixture suite possible.
memory.reason: Reference implementation for how new services should be written across all projects.

memory.title: Interstate supply is CGST/SGST only when supplier state == place of supply
memory.body: If MST_CUSTOMER.STATE_CODE != MST_BRANCH.STATE_CODE the invoice is IGST at the full slab. Same-state is split CGST + SGST at half the slab each. The exception is SEZ customers (MST_CUSTOMER.SEZ_FLAG = 1) — always IGST, zero-rated, regardless of state.
memory.reason: Section 7/8 IGST Act; the SEZ carve-out has burned the team twice.
memory.source: CA sign-off note 2025-06-20 + BUG-883 root cause

memory.title: Tax rounding is per line item, then invoice total — never the reverse
memory.body: Each line rounds to 2 decimals with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, then lines sum to the invoice total. Rounding the total instead of the lines shifts ₹0.01–₹0.04 per invoice and the reconciliation job flags it.
memory.reason: The legacy VB6 module rounded this way and 11 years of posted invoices depend on it matching.

memory.title: Credit note cannot exceed the original invoice net of prior credit notes
memory.body: SP_CreateCreditNote checks SUM(CN.AMOUNT) + new amount <= TRANS_INVOICE.NET_AMOUNT. Over-credit is a hard failure, not a warning — finance treats it as fraud surface.
memory.reason: Statutory audit finding FY2023-24.

memory.title: IPD bill freezes at discharge; only the pharmacy return window stays open 24 h
memory.body: After DISCHARGE_STATUS = 2, charges are read-only except PHARM_RETURN lines posted within 24 hours. Anything later needs a supervisor override with a reason code, stored in TRANS_OVERRIDE.
memory.reason: Insurance TPAs reject bills whose totals change after the discharge summary is issued.

memory.title: Driver cancellation inside 90 s of accept does not count against acceptance rate
memory.body: Grace window exists because the map SDK occasionally assigns a ride across a divider. Cancellations after 90 s hit the rating and the weekly incentive slab.
memory.reason: Ops asked for it after 340 unfair penalties in the pilot city.

memory.title: MST_TAX is slab-versioned by effective date, not overwritten
memory.body: Rate changes insert a new row with EFFECTIVE_FROM; the old row gets EFFECTIVE_TO. Any query that forgets the date predicate picks up 2019 slabs. SP_CalculateTax joins on @InvoiceDate BETWEEN EFFECTIVE_FROM AND ISNULL(EFFECTIVE_TO, "9999-12-31").
memory.reason: Historical invoices must reprint with the rate that was live on their date.

memory.title: TRANS_INVOICE has no FK to MST_CUSTOMER — it is enforced in code only
memory.body: The FK was dropped in 2016 during a bulk-import project and never restored. 1,148 stored procs assume it is absent. Adding it back fails on 4,207 orphan rows from the 2014 migration.
memory.reason: Legacy data quality; restoring the constraint is a project, not a task.

memory.title: Never add a non-filtered index to TRANS_INVOICE during business hours
memory.body: The table is 41 GB / 96 M rows. An online index build still pushed CPU to 94 % and the invoice screen timed out for 8 minutes on 2025-11-30. Index work is a 01:00–03:30 IST window only, with SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON.
memory.reason: Production incident #52.

memory.title: PMI patient identity is (HOSP_CODE, MR_NO) — MR_NO alone is not unique
memory.body: Three hospitals share the schema and each restarted MR numbering in 2019. Any join on MR_NO without HOSP_CODE mixes patients across sites.
memory.reason: Discovered during the OPD dedup task; 1,900 false merges were prevented.

memory.title: SP_CalculateTax is called from 23 places, 6 of them outside the invoice module
memory.body: Callers include SP_PostTransaction, SP_CreateCreditNote, the Crystal report RPT_TaxSummary, the nightly SSIS package PKG_TaxRecon, and two Excel-linked views used by finance. Any signature change is a 23-point blast radius.
memory.reason: Impact analysis for TASK-492 — a parameter add was rejected because of this.

memory.title: The 2011 VB6 tax module is still the source of truth for rounding parity
memory.body: legacy/TaxCalc.bas was ported line-by-line into TaxService.cs in 2018. Where the C# looks wrong, check the .bas first — the "bug" is usually intentional parity with 11 years of posted data.
memory.reason: Two rewrites were reverted for breaking historical reprints.

memory.title: Module 17 (Excise) is dead code but cannot be deleted
memory.body: Excise was replaced by GST in 2017. The screens are hidden but SP_PostTransaction still writes TRANS_EXCISE rows with zeros because a statutory archive job reads them until FY2029.
memory.reason: Statutory retention.

memory.title: Crystal Reports still renders 61 of 88 ERP reports
memory.body: Report changes need the CR runtime on the build agent and a .rpt round-trip through the Windows designer. Agents cannot edit .rpt files — they open a task for the human with the exact field list.
memory.reason: Binary format, no CI story.

memory.title: Session state lives in IIS in-process memory across 3 nodes with no affinity
memory.body: The load balancer round-robins without sticky sessions, so a user whose next request lands on another node loses their session. This is the root cause behind TASK-501, not the 20-minute timeout everyone assumed.
memory.reason: Never migrated to SQL session state after the 2019 scale-out.

memory.title: BUG-883 — CGST/SGST reversed on interstate orders after branch transfer
memory.body: TaxService.ResolveJurisdiction compared MST_CUSTOMER.STATE_CODE against the *login* branch instead of the invoice branch. After the Pune branch transfer in August, 41 invoices split as CGST/SGST when they should have been IGST. Fix is one line plus a backfill migration.
memory.reason: Wrong comparison operand; the login branch is only correct when the user never switches branch.

memory.title: Bulk upload times out above ~28k rows on the shared staging server
memory.body: The chunked endpoint holds one transaction per chunk; at 28k rows tempdb spills and the request exceeds the 120 s IIS limit. Chunk size 2,000 with a per-chunk commit clears it.
memory.reason: tempdb on staging is 8 GB versus 96 GB in production, so the ceiling only shows up in QA.

memory.title: Date pickers send local time; the API assumes UTC — off-by-one on invoices posted after 18:30 IST
memory.body: The React date picker serialises with toISOString(), shifting IST dates back a day after 18:30. Fixed in 6 screens, still open in RPT filters and the ageing report.
memory.reason: No shared date serialisation helper existed until 2026-04.

memory.title: HIMS OPD queue duplicates a token when the print job fails
memory.body: The token number increments before the print acknowledgement, so a paper jam creates a gap and the retry issues a second live token for the same patient. Reception works around it manually at 3 sites.
memory.reason: Print acknowledgement is fire-and-forget.

memory.title: ADR-52 — every transaction write goes through SP_PostTransaction
memory.body: Accepted 2024-11-06, superseding the 2019 "direct write with audit trigger" approach. The trigger version double-counted on multi-row inserts. Status: accepted, no supersession pending.
memory.reason: Auditability and a single place to stamp the ledger.

memory.title: ADR-64 — retrieval is hybrid: BGE-M3 vector + BM25 keyword + graph expansion
memory.body: Vector alone missed exact identifiers like SP_CalculateTax; keyword alone missed Hinglish paraphrases. Final ranking is BGE-Reranker-v2 over the union, top-24 in, top-6 out.
memory.reason: Measured: hybrid lifted answer-correct from 71 % to 93 % on the 180-question ERP eval set.

memory.title: Coding agents run Qwen3-Coder-Next; reasoning agents run DeepSeek-V3.2
memory.body: Kimi-K2.5 is the fallback for both and the primary for the Vision agent. GLM-4.7 handles cheap high-volume work (commit messages, changelog). Qwen3-Next-80B is the researcher.
memory.reason: Cost/quality sweep across 6 weeks of real tasks; the coder model won on diff-apply rate.

memory.title: Worktree-per-task, never a shared branch
memory.body: Each coding agent gets git worktree task/<slug>-<layer>. Merge order is database → backend → frontend, and the reviewer rebases rather than merging to keep the ERP history linear.
memory.reason: Two agents on one branch produced a 3-way conflict on every run in the March pilot.

memory.title: Production incident #38 — ledger drift of ₹18.4 L across 2,106 invoices
memory.body: A 2024 data-fix script updated TRANS_INVOICE.NET_AMOUNT directly to correct a discount error. TRANS_LEDGER was never touched, so the trial balance drifted for 6 weeks before month-end caught it. Recovery took 9 days of manual reconciliation with the auditors.
memory.reason: Direct TRANS write bypassed SP_PostTransaction.

memory.title: Production incident #47 — deploy at 17:40 IST collided with the GST return window
memory.body: A backend deploy recycled the app pool while 60+ users were filing GSTR-1. Deploys are now blocked between 09:00 and 20:00 IST on the 1st–11th of each month, enforced in the pipeline, not by memory.
memory.reason: Statutory filing window.

memory.title: Production incident #52 — index build spiked CPU to 94 % for 8 minutes
memory.body: An "online" index build on TRANS_INVOICE during business hours starved the invoice screen. Trigger for the 01:00–03:30 maintenance window rule.
memory.reason: 41 GB table on a shared instance; ONLINE = ON is not free.

memory.title: InvoiceService.cs is 2,914 lines and owns 7 responsibilities
memory.body: Tax, discount, dispatch note, e-way bill, credit note, print and export all live in one class. The team decided against splitting it during TASK-492 — the split is its own epic with its own regression budget.
memory.reason: PM rule: no unrequested refactor inside a bug-fix task.

memory.title: C# naming here is class-object style: InvoiceService invoiceService = new()
memory.body: Variables mirror the type name in camelCase. Not _svc, not svc, not invSvc. The reviewer agent flags abbreviations as a style rejection.
memory.reason: PM standard applied across all C# in every project.

memory.title: Tests live beside the module: tests/<Module>/<Class>Tests.cs, xUnit + FluentAssertions
memory.body: No NUnit, no MSTest, no Moq — the codebase uses hand-written fakes because Moq broke on the 2022 sealed-class sweep. Test method names read Should_Split_IGST_When_Interstate.
memory.reason: Consistency with 3,100 existing tests.

memory.title: Frontend screens import from @/components/os before reaching for shadcn
memory.body: Layout, density and status come from the OS kit; shadcn is only for interactive primitives. A screen that rebuilds Panel or DataTable locally gets rejected.
memory.reason: Eight themes repaint through the token contract; a bespoke card breaks six of them.

memory.title: ERP renewal is module-by-module; 12 of 47 modules are on the new stack
memory.body: Old and new run side by side behind the same IIS site. A module is "done" only when its Crystal reports are ported or explicitly deferred. Billing is the current module; inventory is next.
memory.reason: Big-bang rewrite was rejected in 2023 after the HIMS v2 attempt.

memory.title: Release train is Tuesday 21:30 IST; hotfixes need a named approver
memory.body: Anything merged after Monday 18:00 waits for the next train. Hotfix path exists but requires the human PM to approve in the Approvals queue with a one-line justification.
memory.reason: Support staff are only available Tue/Wed morning for fallout.

memory.title: FIFA Stats is paused — memory retained, agents released
memory.body: ClickHouse cluster scaled to zero on 2026-09-04. Memory and knowledge stay indexed so a restart does not re-onboard from scratch; do not schedule agent runs against it.
memory.reason: Side project, no commercial deadline.

memory.title: Show the plan before touching a file — every time, no exceptions
memory.body: Agents post a numbered plan with file paths and expected diff size, wait for the approve click, then run. Even for a one-line fix. The PM reads plans faster than diffs.
memory.reason: Explicit standing instruction; violated twice in June and both runs were reverted.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2026-06-03 ("pehle plan dikhao, phir touch karo")

memory.title: Terminal-dense UI, no marketing dashboards
memory.body: Small type, tight rows, flat surfaces, one accent colour. Gradients, glass, big shadows and hero cards get rejected on sight. Numbers are tabular; IDs and paths are monospace.
memory.reason: The PM lives in this UI 9 hours a day and wants density over decoration.

memory.title: Cost ceiling: ₹4,000/day across all agents; local models first
memory.body: Qwen3-Coder-Next and Qwen3-Next-80B run on the local box at zero marginal cost. Paid models are for reasoning and review only. Crossing 80 % of the ceiling pauses autonomous agents.
memory.reason: Single-operator business, no funding.

memory.title: The PM writes requirements in Hinglish — never ask him to rewrite them in English
memory.body: "Invoice mein tax galat aa raha hai — CGST/SGST split interstate orders pe reverse ho raha hai. Fix karo." That is a complete requirement. The Commander compiles it; the PM does not translate. Asking for a formal spec is treated as friction.
memory.reason: He thinks in Hinglish and types fast; forcing English costs him time and loses nuance.

memory.title: Strict SOLID — he will reject working code that violates it
memory.body: Single responsibility and interface-first are non-negotiable for new C#. He has sent back a passing PR because a service did two things. Existing violations stay until their own task; new ones never ship.
memory.reason: 14 years of maintaining a codebase where nobody enforced it.
memory.source: Review history: 23 rejections citing SRP or DIP

memory.title: He hates unrequested refactors — fix the bug, nothing else
memory.body: A diff that also renames variables, reorders methods or "cleans up" nearby code gets reverted whole, even when the fix inside it is correct. If a refactor is needed, open a separate task and let him schedule it.
memory.reason: Review time is his bottleneck; a 400-line diff for a 3-line fix is unreviewable.
memory.source: PM instruction repeated 7 times + 4 full reverts

memory.title: Prefers the existing pattern over a better one
memory.body: If the codebase already does X in an ugly way in 40 places, the 41st does it the same way. "Consistency beats correctness" is a direct quote. New patterns need an ADR and his sign-off first.
memory.reason: He is the only maintainer; two patterns means twice the context to hold.
memory.source: PM instruction, 2025-04-22 ("jo pattern already hai wahi use karo")

memory.title: Tests must actually be run — "tests likhe hain" is not enough
memory.body: Every handoff needs pasted runner output: the command, pass/fail counts and the duration. Claiming coverage without a run is the fastest way to lose his trust; he has caught it three times.
memory.reason: Two agents in 2025 reported green on tests that never executed.

memory.title: Works 10:30–02:00 IST; approvals stall between 03:00 and 10:00
memory.body: Queue HIGH-risk gates before 01:00 or they sit until late morning. He answers Telegram faster than the in-app queue between 22:00 and 01:00.
memory.reason: Observed across 6 months of approval timestamps.

memory.title: Reads the diff, not the summary — keep PR bodies short and file lists exact
memory.body: Three lines of why, then the file list. Long agent-written PR descriptions get skimmed and the actual review happens in the diff view. Never bury a schema change in prose.
memory.reason: Stated preference, confirmed by review-time telemetry (median 9 s on the body, 4 min in the diff).

plans.rawRequirement: Invoice mein tax galat aa raha hai — CGST/SGST interstate orders pe reverse ho raha hai. Fix karo, aur purane invoices bhi theek karne padenge shayad.
plans.businessRequirement: For an interstate sale the invoice must charge IGST against the place of supply. Today the system charges CGST+SGST against the billing state, so 41 invoices raised since 12 Aug carry the wrong tax heads and the wrong total.
plans.technicalRequirement: Resolve tax jurisdiction once, in TaxService.ResolveJurisdiction, from the place-of-supply on the sales order — not from MST_CUSTOMER.state_code. SP_CalculateTax must consume the resolved jurisdiction instead of re-deriving it from the billing address at L288. Existing rounding behaviour is a contract and must not move.
plans.architectureImpact: Introduces ITaxJurisdictionResolver as the single source of jurisdiction. SP_CalculateTax loses a derivation branch and gains a required parameter — a signature change on a procedure with 11 callers, so every caller is updated in the same worktree. TRANS_INVOICE is never written directly (MEM-142); the backfill goes through SP_CommitTaxCorrection.

testPlan: Unit — ResolveJurisdiction returns IGST when supply state ≠ seller state
Unit — SEZ supply resolves to IGST at 0% with the SEZ flag set
Unit — union territory resolves to CGST+UTGST, not CGST+SGST
Integration — SP_CalculateTax honours the passed jurisdiction and stops re-deriving
Integration — invoice total is byte-identical for intrastate orders (no regression)
Regression — legacy half-away-from-zero rounding is unchanged on 2,400 historical invoices
Migration — dry-run 0042 against the nightly snapshot: exactly 41 rows, 0 collateral
E2E — raise an interstate invoice in the UI and assert a single IGST line
openQuestions: The 41 mis-taxed invoices — issue credit notes and re-raise, or amend in place? Amending TRANS_INVOICE contradicts MEM-142.
Two of the 41 are already reconciled in the GL for August. Do we reopen the period or book the difference in September?
Is the SEZ flag on the sales order authoritative, or should it be re-derived from the customer GSTIN? No business rule is documented either way.

plans.rawRequirement: Customer bulk upload chahiye — CSV se, validation ke saath, progress dikhe, aur agar beech mein fail ho to poora rollback ho jaye.
plans.businessRequirement: An operator can import up to 50,000 customer records from a CSV, see per-row validation errors before committing, watch progress, and be guaranteed that a failure part-way through leaves the master data untouched.
plans.technicalRequirement: Chunked upload to a staging table (ADR-49), server-side validation producing a row-indexed error envelope, and a single commit procedure that moves staging → MST_CUSTOMER inside one transaction. No direct write to MST_CUSTOMER from the service layer.
plans.architectureImpact: Adds the first staging-table import in the ERP. The pattern becomes the template for the four other pending bulk imports, so the contract is documented as an ADR before it ships.

steps.label: Research existing import paths
steps.detail: Found 3 ad-hoc importers, none transactional. All bypass the repository.

steps.label: Design staging contract
steps.detail: ADR-49 — staging table + all-or-nothing commit procedure.

steps.label: Staging table + commit procedure
steps.detail: STG_CUSTOMER_IMPORT + SP_CommitCustomerImport with a rollback path.

steps.label: Chunked upload endpoint
steps.detail: 2 MB chunks, idempotency key per batch, resumable.

steps.label: Drag-drop UI + row errors
steps.detail: Blocked behind APPR-120 (papaparse) — hand-rolled parser rejected by the reviewer.

steps.label: Validation matrix tests
steps.detail: Duplicate GSTIN, malformed state code, 64-char name overflow, CSV formula injection.

steps.label: E2E 50k happy path
steps.detail: Must complete under 90s and hold memory flat.

steps.label: Security review
steps.detail: Upload size cap, formula injection, staging table isolation per operator.

steps.label: Code review
steps.detail: Repository pattern, interface-first, error envelope shape.

testPlan: Unit — validator rejects duplicate GSTIN within the same file
Unit — CSV cells beginning with = + - @ are neutralised
Integration — a failure on row 31,204 leaves MST_CUSTOMER byte-identical
Integration — a resumed upload does not duplicate an already-accepted chunk
E2E — 50,000 rows complete under 90s with progress visible throughout
Load — memory stays flat across the whole import (no full-file buffering)
openQuestions: On partial validation failure: reject the whole file, or import the valid rows and hand back a rejects CSV? The operator asked for the second, ADR-49 implies the first.
papaparse@5.4.1 is waiting on APPR-120. If denied, the fallback is a hand-rolled streaming parser — roughly two extra days and a reviewer objection on reinventing a solved problem.

plans.rawRequirement: Users randomly logout ho rahe hain 20 minute ke baad. Production issue hai, urgent dekho.
plans.businessRequirement: A signed-in user must stay signed in for the full 8-hour working day unless they sign out or are idle past the configured timeout.
plans.technicalRequirement: Session state is in-proc across three IIS nodes with no affinity, so every app-pool recycle silently drops every session on that node. Move to a Redis-backed session provider with a rolling restart and a proven revert.
plans.architectureImpact: Introduces Redis as a hard runtime dependency for authentication. A Redis outage becomes an auth outage, so the provider needs a documented degradation path before this ships.

steps.label: Correlate logouts with recycles
steps.detail: All 214 forced logouts land within 4s of an app-pool recycle on the same node.

steps.label: Confirm in-proc session on all nodes
steps.detail: web.config mode="InProc" on 3 of 3 nodes. No affinity at the F5.

steps.label: Stage the Redis provider
steps.detail: Staging held 400 sessions across a forced recycle with zero drops.

steps.label: Production change
steps.detail: Blocked — APPR-118 pending. Production is a human signature, never an agent decision.

steps.label: Degradation path for a Redis outage
steps.detail: Undecided: fail closed (everyone logged out) or fall back to in-proc.

steps.label: Security review
steps.detail: Session fixation, cookie flags, Redis auth and network isolation.

testPlan: Staging — 400 concurrent sessions survive a forced recycle on every node
Staging — failover of the Redis primary loses no session
Security — session id is regenerated on privilege change
Rollback — reverting web.config restores service within one recycle cycle
openQuestions: If Redis is unreachable, do we fail closed (all users logged out, loud) or fall back to in-proc (silent, and we are back to this bug)?
Redis is a new production dependency. Who owns its monitoring and its on-call?

plans.rawRequirement: OPD bill mein 1 rupee ka difference aa raha hai — receipt aur ledger match nahi kar rahe.
plans.businessRequirement: The printed receipt total and the ledger posting for the same OPD bill must be identical, to the paisa, always.
plans.technicalRequirement: Money is rounded in two independent places: BillingService.ComputeTotal (banker's rounding) and SP_PostOpdLedger (half-away-from-zero). Consolidate on the documented ledger behaviour and delete the second site.
plans.architectureImpact: Creates a single Money type as the only place rounding is allowed to happen. Every other call site becomes a compile error until it is migrated — deliberate.

steps.label: Locate both rounding sites
steps.detail: C# uses MidpointRounding.ToEven; T-SQL ROUND() is half-away-from-zero. They diverge on exact .005.

steps.label: Single Money type
steps.detail: Money struct with one rounding policy; 34 call sites to migrate.

steps.label: Reconcile historical bills
steps.detail: Quantify how many of the 1.4M historical bills are affected before choosing a policy.

steps.label: Regression on 90 days of bills
steps.detail: Receipt total must equal ledger posting for every bill in the window.

testPlan: Unit — Money rounds half-away-from-zero at 2 dp, matching the ledger
Property — receipt total equals the sum of ledger lines for 10,000 generated bills
Regression — 90 days of historical bills reproduce their stored totals exactly
openQuestions: Historical bills already carry the divergent totals. Do we leave them, or reconcile? Reconciling touches audited ledgers.

plans.rawRequirement: Surge pricing chahiye — demand aur supply ke ratio pe, per zone, aur 2.5x se upar kabhi na jaye.
plans.businessRequirement: When demand outstrips available drivers in a zone, the fare multiplier rises smoothly, is visible to the rider before they confirm, and never exceeds 2.5×.
plans.technicalRequirement: Per-H3-zone demand/supply ratio computed on a 60s rolling window, smoothed over 5 minutes, mapped through a capped curve, and snapshotted onto the booking so the applied multiplier is auditable after the fact.
plans.architectureImpact: Fares become time-dependent. Every booking must snapshot the exact multiplier and the inputs that produced it, or disputes are unanswerable.

steps.label: Research surge approaches
steps.detail: RES-77 — 14 sources. Smoothed ratio with a hard cap beats a step function on rider trust.

steps.label: Architecture options
steps.detail: Three designs scored by an independent judge panel; ADR-07 proposed.

steps.label: Surge engine
steps.detail: Rolling window per H3 cell, 5-minute smoothing, capped curve.

steps.label: Fare snapshot on booking
steps.detail: Persist multiplier + inputs so a dispute can be replayed.

steps.label: Rider-facing disclosure
steps.detail: Multiplier shown before confirm, never after.

steps.label: Simulation tests
steps.detail: Replay a Friday-evening demand spike and assert the cap holds.

testPlan: Unit — multiplier is clamped at 2.5× regardless of ratio
Unit — smoothing prevents a >0.3× jump inside 60s
Simulation — replayed demand spike never exceeds the cap
Contract — every booking persists the multiplier and its inputs
openQuestions: Should surge apply to the cancellation fee as well? Legal has not answered.
Zone granularity: H3 res 8 is ~0.7 km². Res 7 is cheaper to compute but blurs the airport.

plans.rawRequirement: Memory ko human ki tarah decay hona chahiye — jo use nahi hote wo weak, jo baar baar hit hote hain wo strong. Par jo important hai wo kabhi bhoolna nahi chahiye.
plans.businessRequirement: Memory that gets used stays sharp; memory that never gets used fades and stops crowding retrieval. Nothing pinned or decision-grade is ever lost.
plans.technicalRequirement: Per-category exponential decay with a category half-life, a reinforcement bump on every retrieval hit, and a hard exemption for pinned facts and HIGH-confidence decisions.
plans.architectureImpact: Retrieval ranking now depends on a mutable strength score, so ranking becomes time-dependent and must be reproducible for any past query — the hit log becomes load-bearing.

steps.label: Half-life model per category
steps.detail: Incidents 1460d, human 3650d (effectively never), bugs 120d.

steps.label: Reinforcement on hit
steps.detail: +2 to +7 by category, applied on actual use, not on being returned.

steps.label: Exemptions
steps.detail: Pinned and HIGH-confidence decisions never decay, regardless of age.

steps.label: Retirement threshold + audit
steps.detail: Below 20 strength a fact is archived, never deleted, with a reason.

steps.label: Backtest against 30 days of retrieval
steps.detail: Would decay have hidden any fact that was actually used?

testPlan: Unit — a pinned fact does not decay across a simulated year
Unit — a bug fact drops below threshold 120 days after its fix ships
Backtest — no fact retrieved in the last 30 days would have been retired
Property — strength is bounded in [0, 100] under any sequence of hits
openQuestions: Should a fact that was retrieved but then contradicted lose strength, or is that a conflict rather than a decay signal?

plans.rawRequirement: Discharge summary ke department-wise templates chahiye — cardiology ka alag, ortho ka alag.
plans.businessRequirement: Each department can maintain its own discharge summary layout without a developer, while the clinical fields that every summary must carry stay mandatory.
plans.technicalRequirement: A template registry keyed by department with a shared mandatory-field core, rendered through one printer so pagination and signatures stay identical across departments.
plans.architectureImpact: Templates become data rather than code. The mandatory core must be enforced server-side, or a department can quietly drop a clinically required field.

steps.label: Extract the mandatory core
steps.detail: 11 fields every summary must carry, sourced from the existing printed forms.

steps.label: Template registry
steps.detail: Six department layouts over one printer.

steps.label: Server-side core enforcement
steps.detail: A template missing a mandatory field is rejected at save, not at print.

steps.label: Code review
steps.detail: Round 1 — checking that print pagination is genuinely shared.

testPlan: Unit — a template missing any mandatory field is rejected at save
Snapshot — all six department layouts paginate identically at A4
E2E — a cardiology discharge prints with the cardiology layout and the full core

plans.rawRequirement: Zed se direct OS ke agents chalane hain — editor ke andar se, alag terminal kholne ki zarurat na pade.
plans.businessRequirement: The operator can drive the OS from inside their editor: send a requirement, watch the agent work, approve edits, all without leaving the file they are looking at.
plans.technicalRequirement: Implement the Agent Client Protocol server side: JSON-RPC over stdio, session lifecycle, streaming session/update notifications, and session/request_permission mapped onto the existing approval gates.
plans.architectureImpact: An external client can now start work. Every ACP session must inherit the same permission rules as an internal run — the bridge is the security boundary, so it gets its own review.

steps.label: Map ACP lifecycle to internal runs
steps.detail: session/new → orchestrator run; session/update → the same stream Live Runs consumes.

steps.label: Capability negotiation
steps.detail: fs.readTextFile, fs.writeTextFile, terminal, prompt.image.

steps.label: Permission bridge
steps.detail: session/request_permission must resolve through the existing gates, never around them.

steps.label: Zed integration test
steps.detail: Drive a real TASK-492-shaped edit from inside the editor.

testPlan: Contract — the server satisfies the ACP schema for every implemented method
Security — an ACP client cannot obtain a capability the permission rules deny
Integration — cancelling from the editor actually stops the underlying run
openQuestions: Does an editor-initiated run inherit the project rules of the open workspace, or of the active project in the OS? They can differ.

conflicts.detail: MEM-324 says session state is IIS in-process across 3 nodes with no affinity. The DevOps runbook fact behind MEM-808 claims sticky sessions were enabled at the load balancer in 2025-10. Both cannot be true — TASK-501 depends on which one is.
conflicts.suggestion: Ask DevOps agent to read the live F5 pool config, then retire the loser.

conflicts.detail: MEM-124 pins rounding at line level for legacy parity. The GST slab note attached to MEM-118 (CA sign-off, 2025-06-20) says the statutory method rounds the invoice total. Legacy parity and the statute disagree by ₹0.01–₹0.04 per invoice.
conflicts.suggestion: Escalate to human PM — this is a finance decision, not an engineering one.

conflicts.detail: MEM-309 keeps module 17 alive until FY2029 for statutory archiving. The 2026-08 renewal roadmap behind MEM-801 lists module 17 as deleted in the billing sweep. If the roadmap wins, the archive job breaks silently.
conflicts.suggestion: Confirm with finance, then mark one fact superseded with a date.
